input.prompt:
Read-only analysis of the GPT Researcher repo at ~/scratch-relai/bench/relai-p1 (an LLM research agent: plans sub-queries, searches the web via retrievers, scrapes pages, compresses context with embeddings, writes a cited report). Do NOT edit any file.

Scope: gpt_researcher/retrievers/, gpt_researcher/scraper/, gpt_researcher/actions/retriever.py, gpt_researcher/actions/web_scraping.py, gpt_researcher/context/, gpt_researcher/memory/embeddings.py, gpt_researcher/vector_store/, gpt_researcher/document/, gpt_researcher/skills/browser.py, gpt_researcher/skills/context_manager.py, gpt_researcher/skills/curator.py, plus the relevant config defaults in gpt_researcher/config/variables/default.py.

Goal: find mechanisms by which the research agent produces a WRONG, EMPTY, UNGROUNDED or MISATTRIBUTED report (not ordinary style issues). Examples of the kind of thing wanted: retriever failure swallowed so research continues with zero sources and the LLM writes from parametric memory; snippet treated as full content; URL/source mismatch after compression so citations point at the wrong page; dedup/visited-URL logic dropping all results; silent truncation; similarity threshold filtering out everything; scraper returning boilerplate/error pages (403, cookie wall, captcha) counted as content; PDF/local-file handling; untrusted page text flowing into prompts (prompt injection) unchanged. Verify each claim by reading the actual code; give file:line, the mechanism, a realistic trigger, and the observable failure. Rate each: impact (high/med/low), confidence that the mechanism is real (high/med/low), triggerability. Also note any existing tests in tests/ that already cover it. Distinguish confirmed-by-code from speculative. Return a ranked list of at most ~12 findings, concise, no file dumps.

input.prompt:
Read-only analysis of the GPT Researcher repo at ~/scratch-relai/bench/relai-p1 (an LLM research agent producing cited reports). Do NOT edit any file.

Scope: gpt_researcher/skills/deep_research.py, gpt_researcher/mcp/ (client, tool_selector, research, streaming), multi_agents/ (LangGraph multi-agent pipeline: planner/editor/researcher/reviewer/reviser/writer/publisher, human-in-the-loop), and deep_agents/ (agent.py, tools.py, README/BENCHMARK.md and benchmark_results — check what benchmark results say about failures). Goal: find mechanisms by which these modes produce wrong, incomplete, ungrounded, runaway-cost or hung results. Examples: LLM JSON output parsed loosely so a malformed plan yields empty sections; recursion/breadth without budget; reviewer/reviser loop that never terminates or terminates without changes; MCP tool selection by LLM picking wrong/unsafe tools or tool output injected into prompts; concurrency errors swallowed; deep research learnings losing citations; human feedback ignored; docs promising behavior the code doesn't do. Verify each claim by reading the actual code; give file:line, mechanism, realistic trigger, observable failure, ratings (impact, confidence the mechanism is real, triggerability), and any existing test in tests/ that covers it. Also summarize what deep_agents benchmark results/BENCHMARK.md record about measured failures (cite file). Distinguish confirmed-by-code from speculative. Return a ranked list of at most ~12 findings, concise.

input.prompt:
Read-only analysis of the GPT Researcher repo at ~/scratch-relai/bench/relai-p1 (an LLM research agent producing cited reports, served via a FastAPI/WebSocket backend). Do NOT edit any file.

Scope: backend/ (server, websocket manager, report_type/ including detailed_report and deep research, chat/), gpt_researcher/config/ (config.py, variables), gpt_researcher/llm_provider/, gpt_researcher/utils/llm.py and costs.py, gpt_researcher/actions/report_generation.py and markdown_processing.py, gpt_researcher/skills/writer.py, cli.py. Also read ISSUE_BACKLOG.md (a maintainer triage board, sections on bugs) to find reported failures of the agent's behavior that are still open, and check whether the code at this snapshot still has the mechanism.

Goal: mechanisms by which a user gets a wrong/truncated/ungrounded report, silent failure, wrong language/tone/report type, runaway cost, or unsafe behavior from untrusted input. Examples: detailed report subtopic generation failing silently and producing a report with missing sections; token limits truncating reports silently; config env parsing misreading values; LLM provider fallback errors swallowed returning empty string; chat agent answering without grounding; cost tracking inaccurate; WebSocket params (source_urls, mcp_configs, report_source) letting untrusted input steer the agent. Focus on agent behavior risks rather than generic web security, but note security items briefly if severe. Verify each claim in code; give file:line, mechanism, trigger, observable failure, ratings (impact, confidence mechanism is real, triggerability), existing tests in tests/ covering it. Return a ranked list of at most ~12 findings plus a short list of still-open backlog bugs relevant to agent behavior (issue number, and whether code confirms it). Concise.

RELAI state for the GPT Researcher agent in this repository. `wiki/` lists what the agent
must do (`requirements/`), where it is likely to fail (`risks/`) and the decisions still open
(`open-questions/`). Start at `wiki/index.md`. `STATUS.md` shows where things stand.

The shared guarantees, terms and working rules are in the RELAI plugin's
`skills/start/template/README.md` (version 0.1.0). Only the wiki and its checker are used so
far, so that file was not copied here (see `UPSTREAM.md`). Copy it in when evals are built.
